title: In This Town, at 18 Your House Drives You Where You Belong
description: On your 18th birthday your house drives you to where you belong. Mine didn't move. Then I found out why…

scenes.narration: In this town, on your eighteenth birthday, your house wakes up. And it drives you to where you *belong*.
My best friend Max turned eighteen last spring. His house drove him straight to the beach. He's a surfer now.
My cousin Lily got driven to the mountains. She runs a ski school now. Nobody ever argues with their house.
Every birthday, the whole town comes out to watch the houses roll away. It's the best party of the year.
Yesterday was my eighteenth birthday. Everyone came to watch.
And my house... didn't move. Not one *centimeter*.
I tried talking to it. Nothing. I tried pushing it. Nothing. My mom even honked the doorbell like a horn.
By evening, everyone had gone home. Everyone thought my house was broken. And maybe, so was I.
That night, a storm rolled in. And through the rain, I saw headlights. Coming down our road.
I sat on the porch all night, talking to my front door like an idiot. Please. Just move.
A house. On wheels. Driving toward us. A house I hadn't seen since I was *eight*.
My dad's house. It drove away ten years ago, and he never came back.
My house wasn't broken. It was *waiting*. It knew where I belonged before I did.
Now both houses are parked next to each other. And both engines are running.
Dad wants me to come with him. Mom wants me to stay. And my house is waiting for my answer. What should I do?
